items.primary_i_can: I can explain why force is a vector quantity.
items.evidence_job: Use arrow length and direction as vector information.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.3: force vectors, same/opposite-direction combination, resultant from scaled arrows; Physics Framework: representations carry evidence.
items.student_text: Diagram A shows a 4 cm arrow east; Diagram B shows a 2 cm arrow west, using the same scale. Name the two vector features that differ.
items.student_html: Diagram A shows a 4 cm arrow east; Diagram B shows a 2 cm arrow west, using the same scale. Name the two vector features that differ.
items.solution_text: Arrow length represents relative magnitude and arrow orientation represents direction.
items.solution_html: Arrow length represents relative magnitude and arrow orientation represents direction.

items.primary_i_can: I can explain why force is a vector quantity.
items.evidence_job: Recognize why force requires both magnitude and direction.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.3: force vectors, same/opposite-direction combination, resultant from scaled arrows; Physics Framework: representations carry evidence.
items.student_text: Which description is complete enough to specify a force vector?
items.student_html: Which description is complete enough to specify a force vector?
items.solution_text: A vector needs both magnitude (12 N) and direction (left).
items.solution_html: A vector needs both magnitude (12 N) and direction (left).

items.primary_i_can: I can combine forces acting in the same direction or opposite directions.
items.evidence_job: Combine same/opposite-direction forces in a physical situation.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.3: force vectors, same/opposite-direction combination, resultant from scaled arrows; Physics Framework: representations carry evidence.
items.student_text: A crate has 36 N right and 14 N left. Find the net force and direction.
items.student_html: A crate has 36 N right and 14 N left. Find the net force and direction.
items.solution_text: 36 − 14 = 22 N toward the larger rightward force.
items.solution_html: 36 − 14 = 22 N toward the larger rightward force.

items.primary_i_can: I can combine forces acting in the same direction or opposite directions.
items.evidence_job: Infer a missing force from a desired resultant.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.3: force vectors, same/opposite-direction combination, resultant from scaled arrows; Physics Framework: representations carry evidence.
items.student_text: A cart has 60 N right. What leftward force produces a net force of 18 N right?
items.student_html: A cart has 60 N right. What leftward force produces a net force of 18 N right?

items.primary_i_can: I can identify the resultant force from a simple vector diagram and use arrow length and direction to compare force strength and direction.
items.evidence_job: Read vectors and determine resultant magnitude/direction.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.3: force vectors, same/opposite-direction combination, resultant from scaled arrows; Physics Framework: representations carry evidence.
items.student_text: Scaled diagram: 9 N ← [sled] → 15 N. Determine the resultant.
items.student_html: Scaled diagram: 9 N ← [sled] → 15 N. Determine the resultant.
items.solution_text: Opposite vectors subtract: 15 − 9 = 6 N, toward the larger rightward vector.
items.solution_html: Opposite vectors subtract: 15 − 9 = 6 N, toward the larger rightward vector.

items.primary_i_can: I can identify the resultant force from a simple vector diagram and use arrow length and direction to compare force strength and direction.
items.evidence_job: Check consistency between a vector diagram and resultant statement.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.3: force vectors, same/opposite-direction combination, resultant from scaled arrows; Physics Framework: representations carry evidence.
items.student_text: Diagram: 7 N ← [cart] → 12 N. Which resultant statement matches the diagram?
items.student_html: Diagram: 7 N ← [cart] → 12 N. Which resultant statement matches the diagram?
items.solution_text: The opposite vectors subtract to 5 N right.
items.solution_html: The opposite vectors subtract to 5 N right.
